messages:
Priya (Design): Dropping a new concept for the latency card: a compact p95 mini-card anchored to the heatmap with a tiny 'Capture rate' pill next to the scrubber. Goal: surface sampling without taking too much vertical space. Figma link: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123 (v2). Thoughts on flow & accessibility? Ethan (Eng-UX): Nice visual. Main concern: discoverability if we tuck controls too deep. Users expect sampling near the timeline scrubber or above the heatmap. The pill helps, but make sure it's keyboard reachable and has a clear affordance to open the slider. Maya (Research): From sessions: when sampling affected p95, users wanted to know immediately whether results were sampled or full. Recommend an inline status (e.g., small dot + percent) that reads aloud to screen readers. Also test whether novices understand 'sampling' vs 'capture rate'. Kai (PM): Product constraints: default should be 'sampled' for free tiers to save cost; for enterprise trials default full. We should make default visible on onboarding. Also request a short CTA explaining cost impact: 'Lower capture = lower cost, less accurate p95'. Zoe (DesignOps): Microcopy proposal: label as 'Capture rate' rather than 'Sampling' — clearer for non-researchers. Tooltip: 'Percent of requests included in aggregated views (p95, heatmap)'. Also flag contrast issues for the pill in dark theme at 10% fill. Sam (Eng-Infra): Implementation notes: the heatmap is canvas-based; adding tabbable pill requires extra DOM overlay. Will add a focusable button with role="button" and aria-controls to open slider. Need to ensure drag events are debounced so we don't flood metrics queries. Also backend needs a query flag to indicate sampling meta so UI can display when results are sampled. Priya (Design): Updated mock: pill sits to left of scrubber, shows '10%' and small chevron. Pressing Enter opens a mini popover slider. Shortcut hint 'S' shown on hover. I'll prototype keyboard mock flows tonight. Ethan (Eng-UX): Proposed keyboard tabindex ordering: 1) scrubber handle, 2) capture-rate pill (button), 3) when popover open: slider focus. Slider should support arrow keys and page up/down increments. Add aria-live region to announce value changes while adjusting. Sam (Eng-Infra): Quick code sketch I can test:
Percent of requests sampled for aggregated views (p95 and heatmap)
I'll wire aria-live for announcements and make sure focus is trapped in the popover while open. Maya (Research): Microcopy nit: 'requests' vs 'traces' wording matters across teams. Suggest: 'Percent of requests sampled for aggregated views (p95, heatmap)' — clearer in tasks. Also test the pill color + focus ring with TalkBack/VoiceOver. Zoe (DesignOps): Accessibility checklist: contrast >= 4.5:1 for foreground on pill; visible focus ring (not relying on outline:none); keyboard focus order verified; popover close on Esc; aria-describedby points to description; check touch target size. I'll add items to the review checklist. Priya (Design): I'll update Figma with the new microcopy, put a11y notes, and add an alternative design where the capture control lives in the timepicker presets (e.g., 'Last 1h (sampled)') to reduce clutter. Will link both variants. Ethan (Eng-UX): One more idea: show a subtle badge over the p95 label when sampling is active: 'sampled • 10%'. That gives immediate context when users glance at cards. Could be collapsed on narrow viewports. Sam (Eng-Infra): Backend follow-up: I'll add an opt-in query parameter and a response flag like 'sample_meta': {percent:10, method:'uniform'}. We should version this so older clients don't break. Priya (Design): Perfect. I'll post updated prototypes (pill + timepicker-presets variant) tomorrow. Thanks everyone — will flag for accessibility review once prototype is live :tada: design-bot: New design review created for "Compact p95 capture pill" and assigned to @Priya (Design). Reminder: include accessibility checklist before final approval.
